**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It returns the origin if it matches one of these, and `null` otherwise, which means no CORS headers:

- `http://localhost:4200`, an exact match.
- Any origin ending in `.pages.dev`, at any subdomain depth.
- Any origin ending in `.workers.dev`, at any subdomain depth.
- A request with no `Origin` header gets `null` (`if (!origin) return null`, line 22).

Other CORS settings in the same block:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS.
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization.
- `maxAge`: 86400.

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if (...)` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add another `||` clause with the full origin, scheme included and no trailing slash. For example, `origin === 'https://app.example.com'`.

Don't put the domain in an array form of `origin`. Hono treats array entries as exact strings, so wildcards won't work there. The code comment on line 20 and `docs/code/worker/src/index.md:26-27` both say this. For a wildcard such as all subdomains of a domain, use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`. That also matches lookalike hosts if you drop the leading dot, so keep the dot.

`docs/code/worker/src/index.md` points to DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4 (CORS) for more background. I didn't open it.

I changed nothing.
